articles.title: Ball Horticultural Company: Determination of Nonregulated Status for Red Flower Petals African Marigold (Tagetes erecta) Event pBALL123-022-BE113 3

Project-Level Predecisional Administrative Review Process
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture is issuing a final rule amending its Project-Level Predecisional Administrative Review Process regulations. These regulations establish the process by which the public may file objections seeking administrative review of proposed projects and activities implementing land management plans on national forests and grasslands. The Department is amending these regulations to consolidate and streamline processes, increase efficiency, and better align with the Agency's statutory obligations and recent rescissions and revisions to National Environmental Policy Act regulations.

articles.title: Magnuson-Stevens Act Provisions; Fisheries off West Coast States; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery; Pacific Coast Groundfish Fishery Management Plan; Fixed Gear Marking and Entanglement Risk Reduction
articles.summary: This rulemaking implements gear marking requirements and entanglement risk reduction measures for portions of the Pacific coast groundfish fishery. This rulemaking consists of mandatory requirements and voluntary measures. These new requirements and voluntary measures are established pursuant to the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act). The intent of the gear marking requirements is to increase the likelihood of attributing entanglements to a specific fishery and gear type. The intent of the risk reduction measures is to reduce bycatch by decreasing the likelihood of marine animal entanglements with fishing line.

articles.title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; 2026 Commercial Quota Harvested for the State of Maine
articles.summary: NMFS announces that the 2026 summer flounder commercial quota allocated to the State of Maine has been harvested. Vessels issued a commercial Federal fisheries permit for the summer flounder fishery may not land summer flounder in Maine for the remainder of calendar year 2026, unless additional quota becomes available through a transfer from another state. Regulations governing the summer flounder fishery require publication of this notification to advise Maine that the quota has been harvested, and to advise vessel permit holders and dealer permit holders that no Federal commercial quota is available for landing summer flounder in Maine.

articles.content: China P&I seeks seat at global insurance top table - Splash247 China Shipowners Mutual Assurance Association, better known as China P&I Club, has formally applied to join the International Group of P&I Clubs, potentially bringing a mainland Chinese insurer into the powerful marine insurance grouping for the first time. The International Group confirmed it had received the application after China P&I chairman Xu Lirong and other senior executives visited its London headquarters on October 13. “The Group was pleased to welcome CPI Chairman Xu Li Rong and other senior members of CPI to the IG’s London office,” International Group chief executive Nick Shaw said.“ At the meeting, the IG was presented with CPI’s application to join the IG, which will be considered in accordance with the agreed process.” The application will be assessed over the coming months against admission criteria agreed by the existing clubs. The International Group stressed that the process will not affect the February 2027 P&I renewal. China P&I is not starting entirely outside the system. The Shanghai-headquartered mutual is already an approved reinsured association within the International Group structure and has reinsurance arrangements with several existing member clubs. Full membership, however, would represent a significant step up in its position in the international marine insurance market. articles.content: Tsakos returns to containership contracting in China - Splash247 Hengli Shipbuilding Greek shipping group Tsakos has returned to the containership newbuilding market, emerging behind an order for two 3,200 teu vessels at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries. The pair appear in the Athens-based owner’s latest fleet register, with both scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2028. Both will be scrubber-fitted and equipped with alternative maritime power systems, allowing them to connect to shore-side electricity while alongside. Shipping database records point to contracts signed in September, although Alphaliner said the exact timing remains unclear and that the orders could have been concluded in August or September. Market sources put the ships at around $48m each, depending on final specification, implying a combined investment of about $96m. Neither Tsakos nor Hengli has disclosed pricing. Charter arrangements are also unknown. Alphaliner noted that Tsakos has typically backed containership newbuildings with forward employment, but there is no indication yet whether the Hengli pair have already been fixed. The deal marks Tsakos’ first return to boxship contracting since 2022, when the group booked a series of approximately 2,800 teu vessels at HD Hyundai Mipo in South Korea. articles.content: Falklands offshore development faces new international legal challenge - Splash247 Falkland Islands Govt The dispute over offshore oil development around the Falkland Islands has escalated, with Argentina seeking emergency measures from an international maritime tribunal while the UK moves to protect companies involved in economic activity linked to the islands. Argentina filed a request with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS), seeking provisional measures to prevent the UK from authorising hydrocarbon exploitation on the North Falkland Basin continental shelf. The filing forms part of an arbitration Buenos Aires launched against the UK under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. Argentina argues that continued oil development could undermine its claimed sovereign rights and, while the dispute remains unresolved, risk serious harm to the marine environment. “The Argentine Republic reaffirms, once again, its legitimate and imprescriptible sovereign rights over the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas. By history and by right: the Falkland Islands are Argentine,” the government said in its statement. London responded immediately with plans to use its Protection of Trading Interests legislation to shield UK companies and individuals from Argentine measures targeting activity around the Falklands. articles.content: Despite new record, Port of LA chief warns of tariff-driven planning risk - FreightWaves The Port of Los Angeles moved 1.42 million TEUs in September, its best single month ever and the highest monthly volume ever recorded by a port in the Western Hemisphere, Executive Director Gene Seroka said this week. He said lower tariff levels, resilient consumer demand, and cargo shifting away from constrained Panama Canal and Suez routes drove the surge. Record quarter September imports totaled 546,000 loaded TEUs, up 19% year over year and 26% above the port’s five-year average. Exports rose 10% to 126,000 loaded TEUs, while the port handled a record 371,000 empty containers as carriers repositioned equipment to Asia. July through September was the port’s strongest quarter on record at nearly 3 million TEUs, and June through September moved nearly 4 million containers. Through September, 2026 volume stood at nearly 8.1 million TEUs, up about 3% from the same period in 2025. Seroka said the port expects October volume of about 900,000 TEUs. He cited typhoon-related schedule disruptions in Asia, cargo “roll pools” before China’s national holiday, and continued holiday-season replenishment as reasons volumes should remain elevated. Trade and sourcing shifts Seroka in a media briefing said Vietnam is now the port’s second-largest trading partner behind China, while Thailand has entered the port’s top five for the first time. James Edge breaks down how importers, exporters and retailers are handling tariffs, shifting demand and new data requirements. In this FreightWaves conversation, Edge explains the real operator playbook: split U.S. and Canadian fulfillment, add warehouse capacity inside Canada, and stay ahead of changing customs rules. If you move freight across the border, this is the practical takeaway. #CrossBorder #CanadaTrade #Tariffs Rapidly shifting U.S.-Canada tariffs are compelling importers and exporters to restructure their warehouse networks and sourcing strategies, according to James Edge, CEO of Cross Border at Bnode and chairperson at Landmark Global. Edge, who works daily with retailers moving goods across the U.S.-Canada border, said the unpredictability of policy changes — not the tariffs themselves — has been the hardest element to manage in 2025. The post Mexico truck exports soar 145% as US demand accelerates appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Mexico truck exports soar 145% as US demand accelerates - FreightWaves Mexican manufacturers produced 15,181 heavy-duty vehicles during September, compared with 6,857 in the same month last year. Exports totaled 12,707 units, up 144.6% from September 2025, marking a significant acceleration in cross-border commercial vehicle shipments, according to figures from Mexico’s National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI) presented by the National Association of Bus, Truck and Tractor-Trailer Producers (ANPACT). The September rebound comes as Mexico’s domestic heavy-duty vehicle market continues to struggle with weak sales, delayed fleet replacement decisions and uncertainty surrounding U.S. trade policies. Rogelio Arzate, executive president of ANPACT, said growing demand from U.S. customers preparing for new emissions standards has been a major factor behind the increase in production and exports. “The reason why production and exports are growing at the levels they are is precisely because the United States, our main trading partner, is currently undergoing this technology shift,” Arzate said during an October news conference. OK SEOUL, Oct. 13 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday reaffirmed South Korea's push to develop a new shipping route through the Arctic Ocean, saying it will be pursued in compliance with international norms and sanctions. The president made the pledge at a ceremony celebrating South Korea's successful voyage to Europe through the Arctic Ocean by a container ship, as the country seeks to operate summer-season container shipping services linking Asia and Europe. The PanStar Acro, a South Korean container ship, returned to the southeastern port city of Busan on Sunday after sailing via the Arctic Ocean north of Russia to Britain, the Netherlands and Poland, 50 days after leaving Busan. The pilot voyage marks the first successful trip by a South Korean container vessel via the Arctic Ocean, a route which is riskier due to polar ice, but offers faster shipping than routes via the Suez Canal. Growing international use of the Arctic route has, however, raised concerns that cooperation with Russian entities could undermine international sanctions imposed on Russia over its war with Ukraine. articles.content: Emarat Maritime piles six more tankers onto China orderbook - Splash247 Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry Dubai-based Emarat Maritime has added another six tanker newbuildings to its rapidly expanding fleet, lining up a series of 74,000 dwt LR1 product carriers in China. The company’s own fleet register now lists six LR1 newbuildings, with the first two scheduled for delivery in 2029 and the remaining four in 2030. Shipbuilding database records seen by Splash place the sextet at Jiangsu New Hantong Ship Heavy Industry. No contract price has emerged. Recent comparable Chinese LR1 orders have been running at around $55m per ship. Kriton Lendoudis-led Evalend paid about $220m for four 74,000 dwt ships at Yangzijiang this summer, while Andriaki was linked to 73,500 dwt units at New Times at $55.1m each. On that basis, the Emarat sextet would benchmark at around $330m, although its actual contract terms remain undisclosed. The latest move significantly deepens Emarat’s exposure to the LR1 sector. Its operating fleet currently includes three older ships of roughly the same size — the 2007-built Dubai Diamond and Dubai Gold and the 2005-built Dubai Green. Delivery of the six new ships would therefore triple its LR1 fleet. The deal also takes Emarat’s overall newbuilding pipeline to 22 vessels. articles.content: Sweden frees sanctioned tanker after seven months - Splash247 Swedish Coast Guard Swedish authorities have cleared an EU-sanctioned product tanker to leave the country after nearly seven months at anchor following an investigation into its registration and seaworthiness. The Swedish Transport Agency has lifted an operating ban on the 2007-built, 75,000 dwt Sea Owl I, after confirming that the vessel is now legitimately registered in Equatorial Guinea. The tanker had been detained off Trelleborg since March 12, when Swedish authorities boarded it over concerns about its flag status and documentation. The ship was originally claiming registration in Comoros, which authorities found to be invalid. A subsequent attempt to establish registration under the Cameroon flag also failed verification. The Swedish Transport Agency said it had now received confirmation directly from Equatorial Guinea and had reviewed the certificates and crew documentation required for the vessel to resume operations. The decision removes the Swedish operating prohibition, although the tanker remains subject to EU sanctions. Sweden’s coastguard stressed that the vessel was not suspected of breaching sanctions. Investigations involving two former masters, including allegations concerning false documentation, have been discontinued. articles.content: Bangkok Post - Media experts urge safeguards for Thai PBS Media experts urge safeguards for Thai PBS Listen Small Medium Large Share Facebook Reddit Copy Link Thailand General Media experts urge safeguards for Thai PBS Academics agree public broadcaster needs stronger financial transparency and more diverse revenue sources PUBLISHED : 15 Oct 2026 at 17:31 WRITER: Mongkol Bangprapa Listen Small Medium Large Share Facebook Reddit Copy Link (Bangkok Post file photo) Replacing earmarked tax funding with annual government budget allocations for Thai PBS could expose the public broadcaster to greater political influence, say media academics, who have called for stronger financial transparency and more diverse revenue sources. Public-service broadcasting must remain independent of both the state and commercial interests, offering an alternative to state media vulnerable to political pressure and private outlets beholden to advertisers and owners, they said. The Faculty of Journalism and Mass Communication at Thammasat University held an online seminar on Thursday to discuss media reform, proposed legislation and sustainable funding for Thai PBS. The debate comes amid scrutiny of the broadcaster’s financial management — including a controversy over an audit in progress — and a proposal to replace its earmarked funding, drawn from alcohol and tobacco taxes, with annual budget allocations. The measures, announced October 8 as part of a package of 38 sanctions targets, bring more than 90% of Russia’s oil production capacity under UK sanctions, according to the British government. The latest action also targets companies supplying equipment used in Russia’s missile and drone programs. The sanctions come as London and Washington appear to be moving in different directions on Russian oil. The Trump administration is considering easing restrictions on sanctioned tankers in an effort to reduce record-high freight rates, Reuters reported Wednesday, while Britain is urging its allies to tighten restrictions on the shipping services supporting Russia’s oil trade. The discussions are happening days after President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with a torrent of criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, European countries and some of Trump’s fellow Republicans in the US Senate. Both Zelenskiy and the US senators called that move a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that would provide Russia with revenue to keep funding its war in Ukraine. articles.content: Prologis tops Q3 estimates, raises development starts forecast again - FreightWaves Logistics warehouse operator Prologis beat third-quarter expectations Thursday before the market opened, significantly raising its outlook for new developments. Prologis (NYSE: PLD) reported consolidated revenue of $2.39 billion for the quarter, reflecting an 8% year-over-year increase and topping consensus estimates by 8%. Core funds from operations (FFO) of $1.60 per share were 11 cents higher y/y and 3 cents better than analysts’ expectations. Lease signings in the period totaled 60 million square feet of space for the San Francisco-based real estate investment trust. Leases commenced totaled 55.9 million square feet, a 15% y/y decline. Average occupancy improved 30 basis points y/y to 95.1%, 10 bps higher than the in second quarter. Net effective rent change on Prologis’ portfolio of multiyear leases was 38%, near the company’s full-year goal of 40%. “Customers are running lean on inventory, and excess capacity within their networks has largely cleared,” said CEO Dan Letter. “We see healthy demand supported by e-commerce, advanced manufacturing and the build-out of the data center supply chain.” Table: Prologis’ key performance indicators The outlook for full-year 2026 core FFO was narrowed to a range of $6.25 to $6.29 per share, a 1-cent increase at the midpoint. articles.summary:
If your trucks have been running the same heavy-duty diesel engine oil since roughly 2017, whether you manage a hundred-truck fleet, run a small operation of a few units, or own the one truck you drive yourself, that oil is about to be replaced by something new, because the American Petroleum Institute is rolling out […]

articles.content: The Heavy-Duty Oil Standard Is Changing In January, What It Means For Your Fleet, Your Costs, And Your Equipment - FreightWaves If your trucks have been running the same heavy-duty diesel engine oil since roughly 2017, whether you manage a hundred-truck fleet, run a small operation of a few units, or own the one truck you drive yourself, that oil is about to be replaced by something new, because the American Petroleum Institute is rolling out a fresh engine oil category called PC-12 that takes effect at the start of January 2027, and everybody who buys oil, specs it for a fleet, or just has it poured in at a shop needs to understand what is changing before it shows up at the next service interval. This is not a marketing refresh or a new label on the same jug. It is a genuine category change, the kind the industry only goes through about once a decade. The last one landed in 2016. Before that, 2006. So if it feels like you have been buying the same oil forever, that is because, in category terms, you nearly have. What is coming in January is a real shift in how these oils are formulated, what they are certified to do, and in one important case, which engines they are even allowed to go into. If you sit on the leadership side of a carrier, this belongs on your radar now as a procurement, budgeting, and equipment-planning item rather than a shop-floor detail to delegate and forget. The operation, carried out on October 13 and 14 at an anchorage off Zhoushan, saw the dedicated bunkering vessel Shenghang Yongle supply the 210,000 dwt bulker, the world’s first ammonia-powered dry bulk carrier. The fuel was produced using renewable electricity at China Energy Engineering’s Songyuan green hydrogen and ammonia project in Jilin province, before being transported through Nanjing to Zhoushan. The operation brought together China Energy Engineering, CMB.TECH and Jiangsu Andefu Energy Technology, establishing a commercial supply chain stretching from renewable fuel production to delivery onboard an oceangoing vessel. “The offshore ship-to-ship bunkering model offers remarkable advantages,” said Li Jingguang, chairman of China Energy Engineering’s hydrogen division, noting that future transfers could reach 2,000 or even 3,000 tonnes. Chinese maritime authorities supervised the operation, implementing special safety measures to handle the highly toxic fuel. Mineral Europa, delivered earlier this month, is heading across the Pacific to Australia for commercial operations. CMB.TECH expects 21 ammonia-powered vessels to enter its fleet by 2029, including 18 bulkers. TagsCMB.TE

Korea sanctions list | Yonhap News Agency Go to Contents Go to Navigation Facebook X More Pinterest Linked in Tumblr Reddit Facebook Messenger Copy URL URL is copied. OK SEOUL, Oct. 12 (Yonhap) -- The European Union (EU) on Monday added three individuals and four entities to its sanctions list targeting North Korea over its nuclear and missile programs and ties with Russia. "The Council today adopted additional restrictive measures against three individuals and four entities under its autonomous sanctions list on the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK)," the European Council said in a statement. The DPRK is the acronym of North Korea's official name. The council said the individuals and entities were responsible for supporting, promoting or facilitating activities contributing to North Korea's nuclear weapons, ballistic missile and other weapons of mass destruction programs, as well as for violating and evading United Nations sanctions. With the latest additions, the EU's sanctions list on North Korea now covers 80 individuals and 25 entities. articles.summary: The European Union has imposed sanctions on some of Russia’s most important shipyards, including major submarine builders, naval ship-repair facilities and yards involved in commercial vessel construction, as part of...
articles.content: EU Targets Major Russian Shipyards in Sweeping Sanctions Expansion Smoke rises from a civilian vessel on fire, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Odesa, Ukraine July 19, 2026.Picture taken with a mobile phone. REUTERS/Stringer EU Targets Major Russian Shipyards in Sweeping Sanctions Expansion Mike Schuler Total Views: 117 October 12, 2026 The European Union has imposed sanctions on some of Russia’s most important shipyards, including major submarine builders, naval ship-repair facilities and yards involved in commercial vessel construction, as part of a sweeping expansion of restrictions targeting the country’s military-industrial complex. The new sanctions, adopted Monday, add 826 Russian companies and 743 executives to the EU’s sanctions list. The measures represent the largest single expansion of the bloc’s sanctions listings since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Among the companies named are Admiralty Shipyards in St. Petersburg, Sevmash in Severodvinsk, Amur Shipbuilding Plant in Russia’s Far East, and Severnaya Verf, another major St. Petersburg shipyard. The designations also include Zvezdochka Ship Repair Center, a major facility for submarine maintenance and modernization, and Dalzavod Ship Repair Center in Vladivostok, which supports Russia’s Pacific Fleet. articles.content: Sweden Releases Sanctioned Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker After Seven-Month Detention The sanctioned tanker Sea Owl 1 underway at sea. Swedish authorities have cleared the vessel to leave Sweden after a nearly seven-month detention over registration and documentation irregularities. Photo: Swedish Coast Guard (Kustbevakningen). articles.content: OOCL revenue up 45.1% on trans-Pacific surge - FreightWaves Orient Overseas Container Line reported a 45.1% year-over-year increase in third-quarter liner revenue to $3.28 billion, as higher revenue per container and increased cargo volumes drove gains across all four of its reported trade regions. OOCL handled 2.12 million twenty-foot equivalent units in the quarter ended Sept. 30, up 9% from a year earlier, according to an Oct. 9 operational update from parent Orient Overseas (International) Ltd., itself majority-owned by China’s Cosco Shipping Holdings. Average liner revenue per TEU increased 33.1%. Cargo growth outpaced a 3.6% increase in loadable capacity. OOIL reported that the overall load factor increased 4.2% compared with the third quarter of 2025. Trans-Pacific leads revenue growth The trans-Pacific trade delivered the largest revenue increase among OOCL’s reported regions. Revenue rose 71.8% to $1.44 billion, while container volumes increased 13.1% to 595,139 TEUs. That compared with revenue of $837.9 million and volumes of 526,032 TEUs in the same quarter last year. Asia-Europe recorded the fastest volume growth, with liftings rising 15.4% to 399,162 TEUs. Revenue on the trade increased 45% to $695.8 million. Intra-Asia and Australasia remained OOCL’s largest region by container volume, handling 981,336 TEUs, up 4.6%. Revenue increased 23.7% to $947.6 million. articles.content: Larger UPS air hub in Philippines boosts Asia service levels - FreightWaves United Parcel Service’s new air hub at Clark International Airport in the Philippines is 15 times larger than its predecessor, enabling the express carrier to provide up to two days faster delivery for customers within Asia and improve connectivity across its global network. UPS (NYSE: UPS) spent $80 million on the expansion project, which includes specialized handling areas for healthcare, high-tech and manufacturing customers with time-sensitive and temperature-sensitive shipments. Parcel handling capacity increased to an average daily volume of 46,000, with maximum processing capacity of 15,000 pieces per hour, according to a news release on Thursday. The announcement marks the first time UPS has disclosed the size of the capital expenditure to expand its Clark hub, which now covers 323,000 square feet. UPS now operates 170 flight segments into and out of Clark every week, connecting businesses across Asia Pacific, India, Europe and the United States in as little as one business day. The new hub has also created nearly 600 jobs, the company said. In August, the U.S. Department of Transportation approved the transfer of six UPS flying rights between Hong Kong and Warsaw, Poland, and Hanoi, Vietnam, to Clark Airport to support growing trade flows between the Philippines and Hong Kong. articles.content: West Africa's ore boom meets China's growing VLOC armada - Splash247 Winning West Africa is fast becoming dry bulk shipping’s biggest growth engine, with its mineral export boom poised to absorb the equivalent of another 120 capesizes by 2030. UK consultancy Tradeviews forecasts in a new report that shipments from the region will surge 50% from 2025 levels to 303m tonnes by the end of the decade, with Guinea’s giant Simandou iron ore project leading the charge. Crucially for shipowners, the long voyages to China will magnify the impact on vessel demand. “West Africa looks set to remain the fastest growing long-haul source of dry bulk cargo,” Tradeviews stated. The growth is already evident. The five West African exporters covered by the consultancy shipped 160.1m tonnes in their principal trades during the first eight months of this year, up 25% year on year. Liberian iron ore exports nearly doubled to 10.1m tonnes. Tradeviews expects regional exports to reach 267m tonnes next year, with Guinean iron ore shipments climbing to 45m tonnes in 2027 and approximately 112m tonnes by 2030. Bauxite exports, meanwhile, are forecast to retreat from a peak of nearly 194m tonnes this year to 153m tonnes by 2030 as Guinea pushes ahead with domestic alumina processing. A capesize round voyage between Guinea and China takes approximately 78 days, compared with just 29 days on the Australia-China route.
